title: A ball's flight is a polynomial
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 170" role="img" aria-label="Path of a thrown ball: a parabola meeting the ground at two points" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M20,140 H280" stroke-width="1"/><path d="M50,140 Q150,-40 250,140" class="u" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="50" cy="140" r="4" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="250" cy="140" r="4" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><text x="50" y="158" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">t = 0</text><text x="250" y="158" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">t = 4</text><text x="150" y="36" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">h = 20t − 5t²</text></svg>
back: Height $20t-5t^2$ is zero at $t=0$ and $t=4$: the throw and the landing. Those are its zeros.

title: Zeros on a graph
back: Count where the graph meets the x-axis: two points, one point (touching) or none.

title: Sum of zeros
back: Sum is sad: it carries the minus sign.

title: Product of zeros
back: Product is plain: no minus sign.

title: Polynomial from sum and product
back: Minus the sum, plus the product. Multiply through to clear fractions.

title: α² + β² without the zeros
back: Square the sum, take away twice the product.

title: Conditions on the zeros
back: Reciprocal zeros: product is 1. Equal and opposite zeros: sum is 0.

title: How many zeros?
back: A quadratic has at most 2, a cubic at most 3. 'At most', not 'exactly'.
